audit.summary: Representative-dependent addition invalidates the central vector space and derived zero interpretation; finite uniform-noise training remains an empirical method. Bounded code variant/training-mode defects and NCE constant error identified.

P1 — Decision-equivalence addition is not well defined; derived vector-space claims fail — Counterevidence: AppendixA mixture identity is correct for fixed densities; paper acknowledges arbitrary-logit difficulty and calls zero derivations intuition. Finite-domain uniform noise remains valid.

P1 — Decision-equivalence addition is not well defined; derived vector-space claims fail — Counterevidence: The fixed-density equal-mixture identity in AppendixA is valid. It does not resolve operation independence on equivalence classes. Page3 acknowledges arbitrary-logit merging fails; introducing sets without changing representative addition does not remove that failure. A selected canonical density or a new threshold rule is additional structure, not an established repair. Boolean indicator operations can be valid independently. AppendixF retains addition and includes positive scaling, so its strictly increasing part already retains the counterexample; allowing constant nondecreasing transforms further loses decision preservation. Both p.5 and p.30 disclaim a formal uniform-zero proof, and these qualifications are preserved.

P2 — Two-output CE repository variant compares arbitrary raw logit offsets — Counterevidence: MNIST repository notebook specifies BCE; grouped JamesWeb uses softmax; exact figures historical configuration unverified.

P2 — Two-output CE repository variant compares arbitrary raw logit offsets — Counterevidence: MNIST_repository_source_cells.txt specifies one output and BCEWithLogitsLoss; the common two-output shift argument does not apply there. Its number_of_non_zero_classes=1 also does not match the current helper binary branch==0, so historical execution remains uncertain. JamesWeb.py:38-54 uses softmax and masks a noise-class win; it is invariant to the same additive shift. No blanket claim about Figures41-44 or accuracy validity is retained.

P3 — Trainer fails to restore model training mode after epoch evaluation — Counterevidence: Both baseline/method sharehelper; linearReLU MNIST lacks same consequence; historical notebook100epochs vs script/figure50 not authenticated.

P3 — Trainer fails to restore model training mode after epoch evaluation — Counterevidence: Both compared CIFAR models share the helper; neither direction nor size of relative accuracy change follows without a repaired run. Linear/ReLU MNIST lacks this same mode-sensitive effect. Script/figure50 versus notebook100 epochs and unknown historical code remain material limitations. No evidence that all training or gradients stop.
P4 — Noise-contrastive density formula substitutes k for log(k) — Counterevidence: Could be repaired by redefining a logconstant; score Eq29 unaffected.

P4 — Noise-contrastive density formula substitutes k for log(k) — Counterevidence: Redefining the symbol as a log-density constant can repair the local notation but contradicts its current explicit definition. Spatial derivatives of either constant vanish, so Eq.(29) score is unchanged. Uniform noise on a finite box and equal priors gives a pd>1/V superlevel decision set, not a general theorem recovering full support or an unseen class complement.
The original report's complete scope, counterevidence and unresolved questions are retained below.
